strings.dash.logs.access_body: Fedora keeps two kinds of journals. Your own user journal (your apps, and your Forge services such as backups and gaming mode) is always readable by you. The system journal (Forge Core, hardware checks, Ollama and the rest of the system) is readable by administrators in the wheel group, and by members of the adm or systemd-journal groups. To let another account read it: sudo usermod -aG systemd-journal NAME, then log out and in.
strings.dash.logs.cut: Only the newest lines are shown. Narrow the filter to see more.

strings.dash.logs.sys_none: You can't read the system journal, so only lines from your own services are shown. On Fedora, administrators (the wheel group) and members of the adm or systemd-journal groups can read it.
strings.dash.logs.sys_own: From the system journal only your own messages are shown. Administrators (the wheel group) and members of adm or systemd-journal see everything.
